after.title: Chicago Transit Authority was awarded a $344.8M grant by the Department of Transportation
after.summary: Application purpose: this award is designed to support a series of initiatives aimed at modernizing and improving ctas fleet and facilities as well as preparing the bus and rail systems for future upgrades.; activities performed: fleet replacement: purchase new buses.fleet overhaul: complete necessary overhauls of the revenue fleet to maintain or extend the asset life cycle.station upgrades: purchase and install new public address system communication hub equipment and passenger amenities.escalator rehabilitation: purchase and install new escalator equipment.elevator modernization: replacement of up to two rail station elevators and the full modernization of nine elevators at central administration buildingsubway structure improvements: conduct engineering and design for initial renovation of subway equipment and structure.capital program management: oversee and manage ctas capital construction program including financing obligations for various projects.; expected outcomes: improved service efficiency: replacement of overage buses and railcars will enhance the efficiency and reliability of cta service while reducing ongoing maintenance costs.extended fleet lifespan: overhauling select buses and railcars will extend the useful life of the current fleet.accessibility upgrades: accessibility improvements for rail stations and bus turnarounds will continue to progress ensuring compliance with modern standards and enhancing rider experience.sogr station rehabilitation: ongoing station rehabilitation efforts will result in more modern and efficient stations with improvements to communication equipment to public address system and to escalators..bus and rail facilities: replace full roof at the 103rd bus facility including garage storage area transportation building and the skylight systems. planning and engineering for building and track modification at midway rail shop. security and communication backbone: ongoing phased sogr replacement of cameras at rail stations and the purchase of new camera systems for support facilities. ongoing phase replacement fiber optic cables and network components along the green line.; intended beneficiaries: cta customers: the funded projects will provide far-reaching benefits for cta riders including improved service quality speed safety and reliability.community: cta funded projects will advance modernization and improvements throughout the system with emphasis on safety and investing in communities. making rail stations accessible deploying innovative technologies and rolling stock advancing sogr initiatives for transit stations support facilities rolling stock and securing the system for cta passenger.; subrecipient activities: none: this award does not involve subrecipient activities. Awarded by Federal Transit Administration. Award IL-2026-013, first obligated 2026-09-24, as reported to USAspending.gov.

after.title: Chicago Transit Authority was awarded a $118.5M grant by the Department of Transportation
after.summary: Application purpose: the purpose of this award is to support design for ctas pulaski irving park belmont stations accessibility program (asap) project which will ensure full accessibility including path of travel in compliance with the americans with disabilities act (ada).; activities performed: funds will be used to cover all eligible expenses including cta staff time the designer of record the program manager and the general contractor to support the project. the project will make the stations accessible by adding an elevator at the stations including improved sidewalks and crosswalks that meet ada requirements; curb ramps with detectable warning and signals; an interior stationhouse ramp at pulaski; accessible customer agent kiosk and employee washroom improvements; lighting; new signage; and accessibility-related communication upgrades.; expected outcomes: funding will allow cta to complete the design of the pulaski irving park belmont stations asap project and ensure all customers can access the stations.; intended beneficiaries: the intended beneficiaries of this project include residents of the forest park and ohare neighborhoods and all cta customers that access the stations.; subrecipient activities: none. Awarded by Federal Transit Administration. Award IL-2026-008, first obligated 2026-09-22, as reported to USAspending.gov.
